# Reusable sections and symbols

**VELORYZ Studio · Pages, sections and layout**  
**Audience:** Project owners, designers and frontend implementers  
**Guide type:** Design specification and team-managed workflow

## Purpose

Reusable sections and symbols should be treated as an end-to-end responsibility, not an isolated button. Start by defining what will change, who can approve it and how success will be checked. Reuse, detach, update and dependency behaviour.

This guide covers reuse, detach, update and dependency behaviour. Use it as an actionable design specification and team-managed workflow: verify the current UI and any provider configuration before relying on a control in production.

## Availability and responsibility

The Studio's website and project delivery workflows support page planning and design; a customer-facing page-tree/flex/grid canvas is not verified. Treat detailed layout controls as implementation guidance, not as promised buttons in a public editor.

Before committing time or budget, confirm who operates this workflow: the visitor, the client portal user, a Studio owner, or the delivery team. A feature described in design documentation is not automatically a public account entitlement.

## Before you begin

- An inventory of the desired routes, page purpose, navigation hierarchy and content
- Examples of layout behavior for narrow and wide viewports
- A reusable section and global-element plan
- A short list of measurable success criteria specifically for **reusable sections and symbols**.
- A recovery plan if the proposed change creates a regression.

## Recommended procedure

1. Locate the relevant area or public route. For new projects, establish the brief at /create/; for owner-only content changes, use authenticated Studio Control at /admin. Do not assume a missing feature exists.
2. Define the specific work item for **Reusable sections and symbols**: capture the initial state, user intent, relevant data, permissions, expected output and what must not change.
3. Follow the design and operating decisions listed below. Work in a draft, staging or reviewed project handoff where available; avoid editing live customer data experimentally.
4. Review the effect with real content and realistic viewport sizes. Record any exception and obtain the appropriate approval before a public change.
5. After the change, verify the public outcome rather than relying on a success message alone; preserve a reference to the reviewed version.

## Topic-specific operating procedure

The following steps are specific to **Reusable sections and symbols** and supplement the general workflow above. Apply only the controls and roles actually available to your account or deployment.

1. Identify which section is truly reusable and which content must remain local to a page.
2. Create a clear naming scheme and dependency list before implementing shared components.
3. Test a global change against every dependent page and any translated copy.
4. Do not assume a symbol library exists in the public creator.

### Evidence to retain

- A short before/after record of the actual user-visible change or reviewed deliverable.
- The exact site URL, owner or reviewer, and the approval or release reference.
- Any unresolved limitation, assigned follow-up, and a safe mitigation.

## Configuration and decision points

- Map each intended page to a clear user need and stable path before visual implementation.
- Define section hierarchy, containers and spacing using semantic HTML and modern responsive CSS.
- Keep global header, footer, primary navigation and repeated call-to-action regions consistent.
- Preview changes at common mobile, tablet and desktop widths and with long translated text.

When more than one implementation is possible, prefer the simplest approach that remains accessible, maintainable and compatible with the current source. Note any cost, licensing, privacy, ownership and performance implications before approval.

## Verification checklist

- Every public path has one meaningful page title and an accessible primary heading.
- Navigation reaches all essential routes without forcing users through search.
- Containers do not overflow at narrow widths and media preserves correct aspect ratios.
- Reuse does not accidentally duplicate IDs, headings or interaction handlers.

Also confirm that the result addresses the original objective: **Reuse, detach, update and dependency behaviour.**. Review the customer-visible language, error states, navigation paths and the relevant device widths. A green build or a successful save does not by itself establish a correct production outcome.

## Troubleshooting and recovery

- For a broken route, verify slash conventions and routing before altering links.
- For clipping, inspect min-width constraints, overflow and fixed-position UI.
- For a global region regression, revert the shared component rather than patching each page independently.

When asking for assistance, include the exact public URL or project reference, a concise reproduction path, the expected behaviour, actual behaviour, relevant timestamps and a redacted screenshot if useful. Never include passwords, access tokens or private customer records.

## Related reading

- [Create and configure a page](/docs/studio/pages/create-edit/)

- [Studio documentation](/docs/studio/)
- [Help Centre](/help/studio/)
- [/create/](/create/)

1. Inventory colour, typography, spacing, border, shadow, media and motion decisions in a token system.

- A short before/after record of the actual user-visible change or reviewed deliverable.
- The exact site URL, owner or reviewer, and the approval or release reference.
- Any unresolved limitation, assigned follow-up, and a safe mitigation.

- Apply tokens across headings, navigation, cards, forms and overlays rather than scattering one-off values.
- Design mobile-first behavior with flexible grids, readable widths and safe touch targets.
- Check the result against approved VELORYZ branding without replacing the original motion logo.

- Contrast supports WCAG-oriented reading and visible keyboard focus.
- The 3D V and other original identity marks remain unchanged unless explicitly approved.
- Text zoom and smaller screens do not hide essential controls or content.

- If fonts fail, supply a readable system-font fallback.
- If a responsive state is broken, record viewport and test case before adjusting shared rules.

# Troubleshooting decision tree

**VELORYZ Studio · Troubleshooting reference**  
**Audience:** Users, support agents and maintainers  
**Guide type:** Practical Studio operations guide

## Purpose

Troubleshooting decision tree should be treated as an end-to-end responsibility, not an isolated button. Start by defining what will change, who can approve it and how success will be checked. Identify the affected area before changing settings.

This guide covers identify the affected area before changing settings. Use it as an actionable practical studio operations guide: verify the current UI and any provider configuration before relying on a control in production.

## Availability and responsibility

Troubleshooting must begin with the observable symptom and available logs. Do not report a provider, integration or service as functioning merely because a route or file exists in source.

Before committing time or budget, confirm who operates this workflow: the visitor, the client portal user, a Studio owner, or the delivery team. A feature described in design documentation is not automatically a public account entitlement.

## Before you begin

- Exact page path, timestamp, browser/device and steps to reproduce
- Expected result, actual result and any non-sensitive error message
- Relevant project reference without private credentials
- A short list of measurable success criteria specifically for **troubleshooting decision tree**.
- A recovery plan if the proposed change creates a regression.

## Recommended procedure

1. Locate the relevant area or public route. For new projects, establish the brief at /create/; for owner-only content changes, use authenticated Studio Control at /admin. Do not assume a missing feature exists.
2. Define the specific work item for **Troubleshooting decision tree**: capture the initial state, user intent, relevant data, permissions, expected output and what must not change.
3. Follow the design and operating decisions listed below. Work in a draft, staging or reviewed project handoff where available; avoid editing live customer data experimentally.
4. Review the effect with real content and realistic viewport sizes. Record any exception and obtain the appropriate approval before a public change.
5. After the change, verify the public outcome rather than relying on a success message alone; preserve a reference to the reviewed version.

## Configuration and decision points

- Reproduce with the simplest possible steps and check whether the issue affects one user or all users.
- Identify whether it is a browser/UI, published content, API, authentication or provider problem.
- Test a safe mitigation and document its effect before changing production.
- Escalate with reproduction steps, impact, current status and confirmed next action.

When more than one implementation is possible, prefer the simplest approach that remains accessible, maintainable and compatible with the current source. Note any cost, licensing, privacy, ownership and performance implications before approval.

## Verification checklist

- Reports contain evidence rather than speculation and identify severity.
- The fallback does not leak private information or break other flows.
- Any claimed fix is verified against the original reproduction steps.
- Recurring faults are linked to a durable documentation and regression test.

Also confirm that the result addresses the original objective: **Identify the affected area before changing settings.**. Review the customer-visible language, error states, navigation paths and the relevant device widths. A green build or a successful save does not by itself establish a correct production outcome.

## Troubleshooting and recovery

- If user data is at risk, stop the affected action and escalate securely.
- If a page is missing, check exact route, publication and HTTP status.
- If a temporary workaround is used, document how and when to retire it.

When asking for assistance, include the exact public URL or project reference, a concise reproduction path, the expected behaviour, actual behaviour, relevant timestamps and a redacted screenshot if useful. Never include passwords, access tokens or private customer records.

## Recommended procedure

1. Locate the relevant area or public route. For new projects, establish the brief at /create/; for owner-only content changes, use authenticated Studio Control at /admin. Do not assume a missing feature exists.
2. Define the specific work item for **Release notes and changelog**: capture the initial state, user intent, relevant data, permissions, expected output and what must not change.
3. Follow the design and operating decisions listed below. Work in a draft, staging or reviewed project handoff where available; avoid editing live customer data experimentally.
4. Review the effect with real content and realistic viewport sizes. Record any exception and obtain the appropriate approval before a public change.
5. After the change, verify the public outcome rather than relying on a success message alone; preserve a reference to the reviewed version.

## Configuration and decision points

- Identify the relevant approved agreement, privacy notice or licensing document before publication.
- Record responsibilities for original content, third-party assets, personal data and client handover.
- Separate operational guidance from legally binding terms and signed approvals.
- Review policy changes with appropriate legal or privacy expertise as needed.

When more than one implementation is possible, prefer the simplest approach that remains accessible, maintainable and compatible with the current source. Note any cost, licensing, privacy, ownership and performance implications before approval.

## Verification checklist

- Ownership promises are consistent with written agreements and vendor licenses.
- Privacy disclosures match actual data flows and retention periods.
- Changelog entries contain verifiable dates, impact and any required action.
- Known issues describe a confirmed state rather than invented uptime or incidents.

Also confirm that the result addresses the original objective: **Dated product changes and migration notes.**. Review the customer-visible language, error states, navigation paths and the relevant device widths. A green build or a successful save does not by itself establish a correct production outcome.

## Troubleshooting and recovery

- If rights cannot be confirmed, pause publication or remove the disputed material.
- If policy language is outdated, replace it only after approved review.
- If a published update is erroneous, issue a clear correction and preserve the change record.

When asking for assistance, include the exact public URL or project reference, a concise reproduction path, the expected behaviour, actual behaviour, relevant timestamps and a redacted screenshot if useful. Never include passwords, access tokens or private customer records.
